about: This fill-in-the-blank picture has two halves: in the top half, white outlined text reads "I bring a sort of [blank] vibe to [blank] that [blank] don't really like", with three black bars over the blanks; in the bottom half a man in a black cap and T-shirt leans on a porch railing and smirks back over his shoulder at a road and empty fields. It is a self-roast format about being the one person whose energy does not fit the room, and being quietly proud of it.
origin: The wording began as an April 2021 tweet by comedian Marcia Belsky about bringing a "we should all quit" energy to her job that managers did not enjoy. It went viral, became a snowclone, and picture versions like this one later added black bars for the blanks.
usage:
There are three boxes, one on each black bar. The first is the vibe you bring, written short. The second is the place or group you bring it to. The third is the people who don't like it.

The best captions pair a mismatched vibe with a setting that clearly can't handle it: a chaotic vibe at a quiet library, a "let's just order pizza" vibe at a wedding planning session. Keep each blank to two or three words so it fits the bars.
aka: I Bring a Sort of Vibe
